questions.question: The functional unit of contraction in a skeletal muscle fibre is the

solution.key_concept: The sarcomere is the segment of a myofibril between two successive Z lines. It is the functional unit of contraction.
steps: A myofibril is made of repeating units that are each bounded by two Z lines.
Each such unit is a sarcomere, and it is the sarcomere that shortens during contraction.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Sarcomere
solution.why_not_others: A myofibril is a chain of many sarcomeres. A fascicle is a bundle of muscle fibres. A motor unit is one motor neuron together with the muscle fibres it supplies.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the motor unit, which is a functional neuromuscular grouping, with the sarcomere, which is the contractile unit.
solution.time_saving_tip: Link the phrase 'between two Z lines' with the word sarcomere.

questions.question: During contraction of a skeletal muscle fibre, which of the following keeps its length unchanged?

solution.key_concept: In the sliding filament theory, thin filaments slide over thick filaments. The filaments themselves do not shorten.
steps: Myosin heads pull the actin filaments towards the centre of the A band.
This sliding brings the Z lines closer together, so the sarcomere shortens.
The I band and the H zone narrow.
The A band corresponds to the length of the myosin filaments, so it stays the same length.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A band
solution.why_not_others: The I band, the H zone and the whole sarcomere all shorten during contraction.
solution.common_trap: Believing the A band shortens because the whole sarcomere shortens.
solution.time_saving_tip: A band = myosin length, so the A band is constant.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the head of a myosin monomer?
options: It forms the tail portion called light meromyosin
It masks the myosin-binding sites on actin in a resting muscle
It binds the $Ca^{2+}$ released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum
It acts as an ATPase and has active sites for both ATP and actin

solution.key_concept: Each myosin monomer (meromyosin) has a head with a short arm (HMM) and a tail (LMM). The head acts as an ATPase.
steps: The head and short arm together form heavy meromyosin, and the tail is light meromyosin.
The head hydrolyses ATP, so it acts as an ATPase.
The head has active sites for ATP and for actin, which allows cross-bridge formation.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): It acts as an ATPase and has active sites for both ATP and actin
solution.why_not_others: Light meromyosin is the tail, not the head. Troponin masks the binding sites at rest. Troponin, not myosin, binds $Ca^{2+}$.
solution.common_trap: Attributing the roles of troponin to myosin.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: During contraction of skeletal muscle, the I bands get reduced in width.
statements.R: During contraction, the myosin filaments themselves shorten and pull the Z lines closer together.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: In the sliding filament mechanism, the filaments slide past each other but do not shorten.
steps: Thin filaments slide towards the centre of the A band, so the I bands narrow. A is true.
The myosin filaments do not shorten, which is why the A band length stays constant. R is false.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A is true but R is false
solution.why_not_others: R is false, so options (1) and (2) are ruled out. A is true, so option (4) is ruled out.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that filament shortening, rather than filament sliding, causes contraction.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Binding of a fresh ATP molecule to the myosin head breaks the cross bridge between actin and myosin.
statements.II: $Ca^{2+}$ ions bind to tropomyosin, which then unmasks the myosin-binding sites on actin.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: $Ca^{2+}$ binds troponin to expose the binding sites on actin. Fresh ATP releases myosin from actin.
steps: After the power stroke, a new ATP binds the myosin head and the cross bridge breaks. Statement I is correct.
$Ca^{2+}$ binds troponin, not tropomyosin. Tropomyosin only runs along the actin filament. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement II assigns the calcium-binding role to the wrong protein, so any option calling it correct fails. Statement I is correct, so the options calling it incorrect also fail.
solution.common_trap: Swapping troponin and tropomyosin.

questions.question: The number of bones in the axial skeleton of an adult human is

solution.key_concept: $206 = 80_{axial} + 126_{appendicular}$
steps: The axial skeleton includes the skull, vertebral column, sternum and ribs.
Together these account for 80 bones.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): 80
solution.why_not_others: 126 is the appendicular count, 206 is the total and 22 is the number of skull bones.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the axial and appendicular counts.

questions.question: Which of the following joint–example pairs is correctly matched?
options: Pivot joint – between atlas and axis
Gliding joint – between carpal and metacarpal of the thumb

solution.key_concept: Synovial joints are of several types, each with a characteristic example.
steps: Atlas and axis form a pivot joint.
The knee is a hinge joint.
The joint between carpals is a gliding joint.
The joint between the carpal and metacarpal of the thumb is a saddle joint.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Pivot joint – between atlas and axis
solution.why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) attach a joint type to an example that belongs to a different type.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging the gliding and saddle joints of the hand.

questions.question: Of the 12 pairs of ribs in humans, how many pairs are neither true ribs nor floating ribs?

solution.key_concept: There are 7 pairs of true ribs, 3 pairs of vertebrochondral ribs and 2 pairs of floating ribs.
steps: Subtract the true and floating ribs from the total: $12 - 7 - 2 = 3$.
These 3 pairs are the vertebrochondral ribs.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): 3
solution.why_not_others: 2 is the number of floating rib pairs and 7 is the number of true rib pairs. 5 comes from subtracting only the true ribs from the total.
solution.common_trap: Subtracting only one of the two categories.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Forms the shoulder joint with the humerus

solution.key_concept: Each landmark of the girdles and skull has a specific articulation or feature.
steps: The glenoid cavity of the scapula forms the shoulder joint with the humerus: A-III.
The acetabulum receives the femur: B-II.
The pubic symphysis contains fibrous cartilage: C-IV.
The occipital condyles articulate with the atlas: D-I.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
solution.why_not_others: Option (1) swaps the shoulder and hip sockets. Option (3) swaps the pubic symphysis with the occipital condyles. Option (4) misplaces the glenoid cavity and the pubic symphysis.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the glenoid cavity (shoulder) and the acetabulum (hip).

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the human skeleton are correct?

statements.A: The skull is dicondylic, joining the vertebral column through two occipital condyles.
statements.B: The vertebral column has 26 vertebrae, of which 12 are lumbar.
statements.C: Each forelimb has 8 carpals and 14 phalanges.
statements.D: Cartilaginous joints, such as the skull sutures, allow no movement.
statements.E: Each coxal bone is formed by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis.

options: A, C, D and E only

solution.key_concept: The vertebral formula is $26 = 7 + 12 + 5 + 1 + 1$. Skull sutures are fibrous joints.
steps: A is correct: the skull joins the vertebral column through two occipital condyles.
B is wrong: there are 5 lumbar vertebrae, while 12 is the thoracic count.
C is correct: each forelimb has 8 carpals and 14 phalanges.
D is wrong: skull sutures are fibrous joints, and cartilaginous joints allow limited movement.
E is correct: each coxal bone forms by fusion of the ilium, ischium and pubis.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options (1), (2) and (4) each include B or D, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Assigning the 12 thoracic vertebrae to the lumbar region, and calling sutures cartilaginous.

questions.question: Gout is caused by
options: an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction
accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints

solution.key_concept: Gout is inflammation of the joints caused by deposition of uric acid crystals.
steps: Identify the specific cause of gout: deposition of uric acid crystals in the joints.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
solution.why_not_others: Low $Ca^{2+}$ causes tetany, low estrogen is linked to osteoporosis, and an autoimmune attack on the neuromuscular junction is myasthenia gravis.
solution.common_trap: Attributing uric acid to arthritis in general rather than specifically to gout.

questions.question: An autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction that causes fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle is

solution.key_concept: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction.
steps: Note the key words 'autoimmune' and 'neuromuscular junction'.
These key words point to myasthenia gravis.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Myasthenia gravis
solution.why_not_others: Muscular dystrophy is genetic, tetany is due to low $Ca^{2+}$, and osteoporosis is a bone disorder.
solution.common_trap: Confusing myasthenia gravis with muscular dystrophy because both weaken muscle.

questions.question: Which of the following disorder–cause pairs is incorrectly matched?
options: Gout – uric acid crystals in joints

solution.key_concept: Tetany results from low, not high, $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids.
steps: Check each pair against its known cause.
Tetany is caused by low $Ca^{2+}$, so this pair is wrong.
The other three pairs are correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Tetany – high $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids
solution.why_not_others: Osteoporosis is linked to low estrogen, muscular dystrophy is mostly genetic, and gout is due to uric acid crystals.
solution.common_trap: Linking tetany to excess calcium.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Osteoporosis is associated with an increased chance of bone fractures.
statements.R: Arthritis is inflammation of the joints.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Osteoporosis raises fracture risk through decreased bone mass, not through joint inflammation.
steps: A is true: osteoporosis reduces bone mass and raises fracture risk.
R is true: arthritis is inflammation of the joints.
Joint inflammation does not explain fragile bones, so R does not explain A.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options (3) and (4) fail. R does not explain A, so option (1) fails.
solution.common_trap: Treating any two bone or joint facts as cause and effect.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: Tetany is characterised by rapid spasms of muscle due to low $Ca^{2+}$ in body fluids.
statements.II: Myasthenia gravis is a genetic disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Myasthenia gravis is autoimmune, whereas muscular dystrophy is genetic and progressive.
steps: Statement I correctly describes tetany.
Statement II describes muscular dystrophy, not myasthenia gravis, which is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction. Statement II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Statement I is correct, so options (2) and (4) fail. Statement II is incorrect, so option (1) fails.
solution.common_trap: Interchanging myasthenia gravis and muscular dystrophy.

questions.question: Bipolar neurons, having one axon and one dendrite, are found in the

solution.key_concept: Neurons are classified by structure, and each type occurs in a characteristic location.
steps: Bipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite.
Bipolar neurons occur in the retina.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Retina
solution.why_not_others: Multipolar neurons occur in the cerebral cortex and unipolar neurons in the embryonic stage. Synaptic knobs are axon terminals, not a location for a neuron type.
solution.common_trap: Confusing the locations of bipolar and multipolar neurons.

questions.question: Nissl's granules are present in which parts of a neuron?

solution.key_concept: Nissl's granules occur in the cell body and dendrites but are absent from the axon.
steps: The cell body contains Nissl's granules.
Dendrites also contain Nissl's granules.
The axon lacks Nissl's granules.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Cell body and dendrites only
solution.why_not_others: Every other option includes the axon, which lacks Nissl's granules.
solution.common_trap: Assuming Nissl's granules occur throughout the neuron.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about myelinated nerve fibres is correct?
options: They are enclosed by Schwann cells that do not form a myelin sheath
They are mainly found in the autonomous and somatic neural systems
Nodes of Ranvier are gaps between adjacent synaptic knobs
Schwann cells form the myelin sheath, with nodes of Ranvier between adjacent sheaths

solution.key_concept: In myelinated fibres, Schwann cells form a myelin sheath interrupted by nodes of Ranvier.
steps: Schwann cells wrap myelinated fibres and form the myelin sheath.
The gaps between adjacent myelin sheaths are the nodes of Ranvier.
Myelinated fibres occur in spinal and cranial nerves.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Schwann cells form the myelin sheath, with nodes of Ranvier between adjacent sheaths
solution.why_not_others: Options (1) and (2) describe unmyelinated fibres. Nodes of Ranvier lie between myelin sheaths, not between synaptic knobs.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the locations of myelinated and unmyelinated fibres.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Neuron types and fibre types each occur in characteristic locations.
steps: Multipolar neurons occur in the cerebral cortex: A-III.
Bipolar neurons occur in the retina: B-I.
Unipolar neurons occur in the embryonic stage: C-IV.
Myelinated fibres occur in spinal and cranial nerves: D-II.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
solution.why_not_others: Option (2) swaps the multipolar and bipolar locations. Option (3) swaps unipolar neurons with myelinated fibres. Option (4) swaps the multipolar and unipolar locations.
solution.common_trap: Placing bipolar neurons in the cortex.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about neurons are correct?

statements.A: Dendrites carry impulses towards the cell body.
statements.B: Synaptic knobs at the axon terminals contain synaptic vesicles filled with neurotransmitters.
statements.C: Unipolar neurons have one axon and one dendrite.
statements.D: Unmyelinated fibres are not associated with Schwann cells at all.
statements.E: The neuron is the structural and functional unit of the neural system.

options: A, B, C and E only

solution.key_concept: Check each statement against the structure and classification of neurons.
steps: A is correct: dendrites conduct impulses towards the cell body.
B is correct: synaptic knobs contain vesicles filled with neurotransmitters.
C is wrong: unipolar neurons have a cell body and one axon only, whereas one axon with one dendrite describes a bipolar neuron.
D is wrong: unmyelinated fibres are enclosed by Schwann cells, just without a myelin sheath.
E is correct: the neuron is the structural and functional unit.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): A, B and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options (2), (3) and (4) each include C or D, which are false.
solution.common_trap: Assuming unmyelinated fibres have no Schwann cells.
